title: Hertz line contact: a cylinder pressed on a flat (implicit mortar contact, plane strain)
source: H. Hertz, Über die Berührung fester elastischer Körper, J. reine angew. Math. 92:156–171, 1882; K. L. Johnson, Contact Mechanics, Cambridge University Press 1985, §4.3 (two-dimensional contact of cylindrical bodies, eqs. 4.45–4.49): b = √(4PR/(πE*)), p₀ = 2P/(πb), with 1/E* = 2(1 − ν²)/E for two bodies of one material and R the cylinder's radius on a flat

quantities.quantity: the largest contact pressure p₀ (at x = 0)
quantities.reason: p₀ = 2P/(πb) for the load per length P = 2265.57 N/mm, b = 0.5 mm; the contact width spans seven elements of the graded mesh

quantities.quantity: the force across the contact (half model, 1 mm thick)
quantities.reason: the pressure carries the whole load; the soft springs that hold the indenter before contact take a millionth

quantities.quantity: the contact pressure at the secondary node at x = 0.29594 (node 7)
quantities.reason: p₀ √(1 − x²/b²) at the node; the nodal pressure (the node's normal force over the area it carries) averages the distribution over the node's elements

quantities.quantity: the contact pressure at the secondary node at x = 0.36701 (node 8)
quantities.reason: as at node 7, nearer the edge, where the elements round off the square-root fall of the pressure to zero at b

quantities.quantity: the contact pressure at the secondary node at x = 0.63325 (node 11, beyond the half-width b = 0.5)
quantities.reason: outside the contact the surfaces are apart: no pressure (an element beyond b, since the edge element carries part of the last closed node's pressure)

quantities.quantity: the vertical stress σ_yy under the centre of contact at depth 0.47127 (node 713)
quantities.reason: σ_z = −p₀ / √(1 + z²/b²) on the axis of a half-plane (Johnson 1985, eq. 4.49); the foundation is ten half-widths wide and deep, not a half-plane, and the stress is the nodal average of the elements around the node
